title: New Jersey's 6th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 general election for New Jersey's 6th Congressional District pits 38-year incumbent Frank Pallone Jr. (D) against Republican challenger Hillary Herzig. The district covers parts of Middlesex and Monmouth Counties, including Edison, New Brunswick, Perth Amboy, Asbury Park, and Long Branch. Registered Democrats outnumber Republicans roughly 2-to-1 in the district, which Cook Political Report rates as Solidly Democratic. Pallone, the Ranking Member on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, emphasizes health care affordability, climate action, and protecting democratic institutions, while Herzig focuses on lowering taxes, parental rights in education, medical freedom, and immigration enforcement.
polling_note: No publicly available general election polls were found for this race as of mid-2026. The Cook Political Report rates the district as Solidly Democratic.

candidates.name: Frank Pallone Jr.
candidates.summary: Frank Pallone Jr. is the incumbent U.S. Representative for New Jersey's 6th Congressional District, first elected in 1988. He serves as the Ranking Member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee and was instrumental in passing the Affordable Care Act, the Inflation Reduction Act, and the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. Pallone focuses his campaign on lowering health care and prescription drug costs, combating climate change, protecting reproductive rights, and defending democratic institutions.

candidates.name: Hillary Herzig
candidates.summary: Hillary Herzig is a Republican candidate for U.S. House in New Jersey's 6th District and a first-time office seeker. She is a Monmouth County native, mother of three, and spouse of a U.S. Army veteran who has worked as a career civil servant across multiple federal agencies including the U.S. Army, Department of Defense Education Activity, Veterans Administration, USDA, and USCIS. Her campaign priorities include lowering taxes, protecting parental rights in education, medical freedom, securing the border, and supporting veterans and seniors.

forecast.rationale: No public general-election polling is available for this race, which limits confidence. However, structural indicators are overwhelming: the district has roughly a 2-to-1 Democratic voter registration advantage, Cook Political Report rates it Solidly Democratic, and 38-year incumbent Frank Pallone Jr. (Ranking Member on House Energy and Commerce Committee) enjoys deep name recognition against a first-time Republican challenger. The combination of extreme partisan lean, long incumbency, and no evidence of competitive dynamics makes this a safe Democratic hold with a wide expected margin.
